headline: European natural gas prices elevated at $16-17/MMBtu with structural supply deficit likely to persist well beyond any short-term geopolitical resolution.
reasoning: Gas storage in Europe was at five-year lows entering 2026, and the Middle East conflict triggered LNG supply curtailments that doubled prices within days to $16-17/MMBtu. Futures contracts through year-end remain at similar levels. The EU is pressing Hungary and others to fully exit Russian pipeline gas by end-2027, further entrenching the structural supply gap that began with the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
quote: The large scale macro fundamentals here for Europe is really the lack of domestic production, probably an almost immediate increase in natural gas prices once the implications of Iran and curtailments of LNG into the region were realized that was probably one or two days and prices essentially doubled.
episode_title: Discussion with Dr. Paul Clarke | CanCambria Energy (TSXV:CCEC)

headline: Hungary's 2% royalty on unconventional production and stable fiscal terms make it an exceptionally attractive jurisdiction for small-cap oil and gas development.
reasoning: Hungary offers a 2% royalty rate for unconventional producers, allowing operators to retain 98% of produced volumes, which Clarke says is unlike any other basin he has encountered. Corporate tax is 9%, permitting is completed in weeks, and land access costs are low given the open agricultural terrain. Policy terms are stable and the government is actively encouraging domestic production to replace Russian imports.
quote: Probably the most attractive, I would say, in Hungary, is the 2% royalty burden that comes with unconventional. So the government there, the ministries there, they recognize unconventional are technically challenging... meaning that we get to retain, keep and sell 98% of the product that we produce.
episode_title: Discussion with Dr. Paul Clarke | CanCambria Energy (TSXV:CCEC)
